How much is a used The North Face Nuptse jacket worth?

The North Face Nuptse puffer sells all winter, and prices rise when it gets cold. Fakes are common, so check before you buy.

Updated 2026-11-06 · by FlipLens

Which one do you have?

The 1996 Retro Nuptse is the classic version. The inside label shows the model and size; genuine jackets have a hologram or a QR code on recent labels, depending on age. Kids' versions and other puffers (for example Himalayan) are different products.

What decides the price

  • Model: 1996 Retro Nuptse and special editions above basic puffers.
  • Size and colour: black sells fastest; bright colours vary.
  • Down: lost loft, leaking feathers and flat spots lower the price.
  • Authenticity: check the labels, the logo embroidery and the zips.

Check before you buy

  • Check labels, zip brand and logo stitching against a genuine jacket.
  • Squeeze the baffles: they should spring back evenly.
  • Look for tears, stains and repairs.

Where it sells best

Sells best from October to February on Vinted and eBay. Buy in summer, sell in winter.

Today's price

Prices for a used The North Face Nuptse jacket change every week, so this page gives no fixed numbers. Questions

How much is a used The North Face Nuptse jacket worth?

It depends on model, size, colour, down condition and authenticity. Prices change weekly, so check today's value: type "The North Face Nuptse jacket" and the condition into FlipLens (fliplens.eu), which compares current eBay listings in the UK and five EU countries and shows the expected sale price and the most worth paying.

When is the best time to sell a Nuptse jacket?

In autumn and winter, when demand is highest. Buying out of season is cheaper.

How can I spot a fake Nuptse?

Compare the labels, the logo embroidery, the zips and the stitching with a genuine jacket. Fakes often have uneven logos and thin filling.
